title: Merge k Sorted Lists
description:
You are given an array of `k` singly linked lists `lists`, where each linked list is sorted in non-decreasing order.

Merge all the linked lists into one sorted singly linked list and return its head. If `lists` is empty or every linked list in `lists` is empty, return `null` (`None` in Python).
constraints: lists[i] is sorted in non-decreasing order.
The sum of lists[i].length will not exceed 10^4.
hints: Merging lists one by one into an accumulator takes O(N * k) time in the worst case, where N is the total number of nodes.
Either maintain a min-heap of size at most k holding the current head of each non-empty list, or pair up lists and merge them in log2(k) rounds (divide and conquer).
Iterative bottom-up pairwise merging runs in O(N log k) time and O(1) auxiliary space.

examples.explanation: An empty array of lists has no nodes, so return null.
Empty sublists are ignored while [-2, -1] and [0, 3] merge into [-2, -1, 0, 3].
